newsitem.title: USA: Russian deputy minister sees uptick in oil output.
newsitem.headline: Russian deputy minister sees uptick in oil output.

text.p: Russia's Deputy Minister of Fuel and Energy forecast a modest rise in his country's total oil production for 1997, but said the government must cut high taxes to encourage more development

"The plan for 1997 was 300 million tonnes (2.2 billion barrels) and it will be a little bit exceeded by approximately three million tonnes (22 million barrels)," Valery Garipov, the deputy minister, told Reuters in an interview during a petroleum conference this week in Los Angeles.
In an earlier speech to oil engineers and investors, Garipov said Russia's economic situation, particularly taxes, had a "bad influence" on its domestic oil sector.
"It is necessary to decrease taxes to 30 to 40 percent, this way we can attract investments," Garipov said, noting the oil tax component is currently 60 to 70 percent in Russia.
He said a new tax code, scheduled be passed by Russia's legislature by 1998, will lower taxes to 30 percent for the cash-strapped oil industry.

Garipov said the recent passage of Russia's new "Agreements on Production Partition" law will allow production sharing agreements between foreign companies and Russian oil firms. He hoped 20 new projects would result from the law by year end.
Output from Russian oil companies with foreign investment stood at 23.7 million tonnes of oil in 1996, and Garipov expects the rate to reach 29.7 million tonnes this year.
Over the next three to four years, the new law will allow about 20 to 25 production sharing projects to start annually, he told the audience.
The production sharing agreements should attract about $12 billion in foreign investment, somewhat below its internal goals.
Separately, Garipov said he hoped Russia will win a bid to supply generators for China's huge Three Gorges hydroelectric project.
"We would like to get it and most likely we'll get it," Garipov said.
